title: `in` against a Flow input is ordinary evaluation even though its runtime operand is on the right
notes: WHAT CHANGED AND WHY. Until 2026-08-31 this case declared SMITHERS4111 at 9:25 and both backends refused the program. That refusal was a WALL: `poc/src/durable/source-compiler.ts` and `compiler/forkbridge/durable.go.txt` each walked a never-executed body into nine Plan node kinds, and SMITHERS4111 fired wherever that walk had no node kind for what the author wrote. The previous note rested on two quotations and they did not fare the same way, which is worth stating exactly rather than summarising. specification/durable-execution.mdx Flow Purity, 'Runtime-dependent control flow MUST be represented explicitly in Plan IR. The compiler MUST reject an operation that would inspect a symbolic value without a corresponding IR representation', is withdrawn ENTIRELY and appears nowhere in the normative text; the Amendment Record carries it under 'Withdrawn -- the Plan IR representation obligation'. The second quotation was two sentences and only its FIRST is withdrawn: 'The compiler MUST lower the function's checked syntax, control flow, and data flow into Plan IR' is gone, while 'It MUST NOT invoke the source function with proxy or symbolic JavaScript values to discover the graph' SURVIVES at Flow and was strengthened with 'at any phase, including replay'. So the technique the old note named as the danger is still forbidden; what went is the obligation to draw a Plan. What replaced them is Flow, 'Ordinary control flow -- branches, loops, let bindings, closure capture, and recursion -- MUST execute unchanged inside a Flow', and Flow Determinism, whose obligations are about what a running body may OBSERVE rather than about what a lowering can draw. So the true cause of this flip is not that a rule was relaxed for this program. It is that the rule was an obligation on an artifact this path no longer produces. The Plan lowerer does not refuse this body; it DECLINES it -- `PlanUnrepresentable` in the reference, `planUnrepresentable()` in the fork, neither of which reports anything -- and the Flow descriptor is built from the Effect Manifest instead. Line 1 of the stdout is exactly that distinction: `effect-manifest` says the Plan lowerer declined, where `static-plan-artifact` -- still printed, unchanged, by 17-durable/a-single-action-flow-lowers-to-a-static-plan -- says it did not. THIS IS NOT A GENERAL RELAXATION, and four cases beside this one prove it: `an-opaque-durable-argument-is-rejected` (SMITHERS4103) and the three SMITHERS4110 boundary refusals were re-run through the same change and still refuse, at the same codes and positions. Those are rules about the durable CODEC CONTRACT, which the pivot does not touch; the six withdrawn walls were rules about the shape of a lowering, which it deletes. HOW IT IS OBSERVED NOW, AND WHY THE .sm IS BYTE-IDENTICAL. An `expect: "output"` case is executed through an exported `main()`, and this program has none -- it exports a Flow declaration and nothing else. Giving it one would edit the program under test, which is the one edit a case may never make in order to pass itself, so the observation lives in a sibling module declared as this case's `entry` and the case's own `.sm` bytes are unchanged. Every line below was measured on BOTH backends and is byte-identical between them; neither was measured and the other assumed. NOT VACUOUS, and the operand asymmetry is still why this program is written separately. `in` is the member of the family whose runtime operand is on the RIGHT (`"mode" in input`), so a walk that only inspected the left-hand side of a binary expression would have found a string literal and seen nothing. There is no such walk now, and the case's job moved: it says that a program whose Action input is computed by an operator over the Flow input still reaches the Manifest with that Action named, line 3.
